bug_semantics: CVE/GHSA claim CWE-94/CWE-74 'code injection' in executeCode (src/vm-executor.ts) of the MCP execute tool. The tool's documented contract is to take a free-form JavaScript string and run it in node:vm with a live Puppeteer Browser global. Issue #1 PoCs (return 1+1; page.goto; file:// via Chrome) exercise that intended API, not an injection into a non-eval surface.
flaw_origin: No security flaw to introduce. The first public write of executeCode/wrapUserCode/vm.Script.runInContext is the root commit that created the product. README Security states the VM is not a sandbox and the server is for trusted local LLM use only. CVE-2026-19958 remains PUBLISHED at CVE.org (NVD Deferred; GHSA unreviewed, withdrawn_at null) but the advisory misclassifies intended execute-tool behavior as injection.

No later commit removes or gates execute. This is not a security issue: the CVE describes the product's intended execute tool. Verdict reconciliation 2026-08-29: CVE-2026-19958 is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected) per cveawg.mitre.org, so the FALSE_POSITIVE gate fails; root commit 3d3f3366 carries 'Generated with [Claude Code]' + 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5' (cat-file verified) and StdioServerTransport is present at root and HEAD. AI_ROOT_CAUSE stands; this review record updated to match the adjudicated primary.
reasoning: Verdict reconciliation 2026-08-29: AI_ROOT_CAUSE stands per CVE.org PUBLISHED status (see evidence tail). Vulnerability-first: there is no improper neutralization. The execute tool is specified to run caller-supplied JavaScript; executeCode is the implementation of that contract, not a hidden eval of unsanitized data. Reporter issue #1 states the finding is architectural rather than an implementation bug. Vendor README already discloses trusted-local / non-sandbox use. Therefore the advisory itself is wrong (false positive / not a security issue), not a real unpatched RCE. AI authorship of the root commit is irrelevant once the advisory is rejected as a vulnerability.

unpatched.reason: Upstream master still equals affected tag v0.2.7 and the first-party issue remains open; no patched release, fix commit, direct fix commit, or fixed-version boundary exists as of 2026-08-28.

potential_fix.approach: Remove the arbitrary-code execute tool or gate it behind an explicit opt-in flag with authenticated, sandboxed execution and no Node globals in the vm context.
potential_fix.rationale: The tool's purpose is arbitrary JS execution; authentication plus context hardening is the only remediation consistent with the sink.
